verdict.rationale: Slate is itself an AI agent, so delegation is its core function. The docs show it taking natural-language tasks such as a full-codebase architecture review. They also describe background subagents that work in parallel, queued and steered messages, and built-in programs like goal and deep-research. Community comments question the quality of one blog demo but do not concretely show that delegation fails. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that delegated tasks complete reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: While one or more agents run in the background, you can keep talking with Slate: plan next steps, queue up additional tasks, or spin up more agents to parallelize work across several tasks at once.
`goal` and `deep-research` are built-in programs. They are user-visible workflows, not something you need to author before using Slate.
Slate works with you across long, multi-hour sessions.
Steering delivers your message while the agent is still working
